sentences.text: 1 Perusal of the record shows that a first information report has been lodged with the allegation that the informant belongs to scheduled caste category and is presently engaged in NTPC.
As the informant was in requirement of an accommodation, the accused persons showed a house to him for which the informant paid Rs. 6 Lakh as advance out of total consideration of Rs. 21 Lakh.

However,
the informant could not understand the malicious intention of the accused persons.

Prior to getting the sale deed of the house executed, the informant tried to find out the details of the house in question and came to know that said house is disputed as it is situated on a pond and a case under Section 122-B of U.P.Z.A. & L.R. Act is pending with respect to said property, therefore, he requested the accused persons to return his money.
The accused persons did not return the money and used caste indicative words and unparliamentary language as also threatened for dire consequences, in case he again requests for returning the money.
After investigation, a chargesheet has been submitted on 23.06.2016 in which applicants have been summoned.

Record reveals that some unregistered agreement to sale of land which is CD Parcha No. 1, dated 16.10.2014 is there, wherein the opposite party no. 2 has agreed to get the sale deed executed whenever he has money.

It appears that after coming to know that the house is situated on a pond and some case is pending, a legal notice was given by the opposite party no. 2 on 12.01.2015 through his advocate, which has been replied by Smt. Nutanlata Pandey (applicant no. 2).

In the petition, the applicants have taken a ground that as per agreement a sale deed was to be executed within three months and after expiry of three months, the earnest money as paid by the opposite party no. 2 would not be returned (though the agreement, annexed as Annexure-4 does not contain any such condition), therefore, prayer has been made to quash the proceedings as the dispute is of civil in nature.

Learned counsel for the opposite party no. 2, on the other hand, submits that the applicants were ready to return the money and has given a cheque of Rs. 10 Lakh, when it was presented before the Bank, it was dishonored.

He further submits that the offence under the relevant sections is made out as there is no condition in the agreement that in case the sale deed is not executed within three months, the money paid by the opposite party no. 2 would not be returned.
Even otherwise, the opposite party no. 2 has been cheated for taking money for such a house which is disputed as the same is constructed upon a pond land and some litigation is also pending.
Learned counsel appearing for the State submits that all the pleadings taken by the applicants relate to disputed questions of fact.

On the basis of material on record after conducting of statutory investigation under Chapter XII Cr.P.C. by the investigating officer, a strong prima facie case is made out against the applicants for the commission of the alleged incident.

In support of his case,
learned counsel for the State has placed reliance upon the judgments of the Apex Court in the case of Dilbag Rai Vs. State of Haryana & Others reported in AIR 2019 (SC) 693 and Central Bureau of Investigation Vs. Arvind Khanna reported in MANU/SC/1432/2019.

sentences.text: In view of the aforesaid, this Court does not deem it proper, and therefore cannot be persuaded to have a pre-trial before the actual trial begins.

A threadbare discussion of various facts and circumstances, as they emerge from the allegations made against the accused, is being purposely avoided by the Court for the reason, lest the same might cause any prejudice to either side during trial.

But it shall suffice to observe that the perusal of the F.I.R. and the material collected by the Investigating Officer on the basis of which the charge sheet has been submitted makes out a prima facie case against the accused at this stage and there appears to be sufficient ground for proceeding against the accused.

I do not find any justification to quash the charge sheet or the proceedings against the applicants arising out of them as the case does not fall in any of the categories recognized by the Apex Court which may justify their quashing.

The prayer for quashing the impugned charge-sheet dated 23.06.2016 and order dated 25.09.2023 as well as the entire proceedings of the aforesaid case is refused, as I do not see any abuse of the court's process at this pre-trial stage.
The present application has no merit and is, accordingly, rejected.
